blocks.content: Waves are generated mainly by wind. Their erosional power depends on height, frequency, and fetch (distance over which wind blows).

cells: High, steep waves; strong backwash causing erosion.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Waves act as the dominant geomorphic agent along coastal regions through erosion, transportation, and deposition.
Wave erosion processes include hydraulic action, abrasion, attrition, and corrosion/solution.
Erosional coastal landforms comprise sea cliffs, wave-cut platforms, sea caves, sea arches, stacks, and stumps.
Depositional coastal landforms include beaches, sand bars, spits, tombolos, and coastal lagoons.

blocks.content: • Swash – forward movement of water onto shore.
• Backwash – return flow of water to sea.

items: Frequently tested: Sequential evolution of wave-erected landforms (Sea Cave → Sea Arch → Stack → Stump).
Differentiate between Constructive Waves (strong swash, builds beaches) and Destructive Waves (strong backwash, erodes coasts).
Identify depositional features like Tombolos (sandbars connecting an island to the mainland) versus Spits.

blocks.content: • Fetch – distance wind travels over water.
• Longshore Drift – zigzag movement of sediments along the coast.
